judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the footer credit line "Hospital de Amor – Desenvolvido pela Williarts" (13px, weight 500). The live CSS sets .et_pb_text_4_tb_footer.et_pb_text{color:rgba(21,21,21,0.2)!important}, and the footer section's background image (Grupo-1595.jpg) is only a 6px colour strip at the top, so the text sits on white. Blended, that is about #d0d0d0 on #ffffff, 1.54:1, far below 4.5:1, which is what the claim says; the snapshot's #14141433 instead of #15151533 changes nothing. A designer credit is real text, not decoration or a logotype, so no 1.4.3 exception applies. The live HTML and CSS match the snapshot. The cookie banner covers this line in the full-page screenshot, but users get the same banner, and once it is dismissed the text is on white. Capture difference: no. The claim names the real failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the top-level menu item "Transparência" (href="#") in the main nav. It is a parent item whose own list item holds the nested submenu (Relatórios Anuais, Balanços Patrimoniais e Subvenções Públicas, Doações Alimentícias, Leilões, Estatuto Social, Membros dos Conselhos, Transparência Cora). The "3" in the browser name is Divi's icon-font dropdown chevron (CSS generated content), not link text. The claim is false of the capture: the same list item, which is programmatically determined context, plainly shows the link's purpose, which is to open the site's transparency section. So it is not true that nothing around it tells. Read with that context, the purpose can be determined, and 2.4.4 is met. A link used as a submenu toggle with href="#" and no expanded state, plus the stray "3" in its name, are 4.1.2 / 1.3.1 matters, not 2.4.4. The live HTML matches the snapshot. Rampa had the list item text and still judged it wrong.
